boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Portland, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A calm, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence that begins with campus orientation, makes room for food and activity, and ends with a nearby riverfront walk.

cards.title: Start by finding the Bluff
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · campus orientation stop
cards.notes: Open the official map before heading out. Use it to locate key buildings, accessible entrances, transit stops, and visitor information around the Bluff.
cards.short_summary: Get the lay of the land before choosing your next stop.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland publishes an updated campus map and an interactive campus map for visitors and the campus community.
cards.access_notes: Use the official interactive map for current building and resource details.

cards.title: Make Clark Library your landmark
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · campus hub
cards.notes: Walk to Clark Library and use its central location as a reset point. It is a practical place to identify nearby academic and student-life destinations.
cards.short_summary: A central campus landmark for getting oriented.
cards.evidence_claim: The University’s Weekend on The Bluff schedule describes Clark Library as a campus hub for studying, group meetings, printing, scanning, and equipment checkout.
cards.source_title: Weekend on The Bluff Sample Schedule
cards.access_notes: Check current library access and service availability before relying on specific services.

cards.title: Pause for a campus meal
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Bauccio Commons
cards.notes: Choose a meal or snack break at Bauccio Commons, then use the dining room as a natural meet-up before continuing through the evening.
cards.short_summary: A meal-plan dining stop on the Bluff.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland identifies Bauccio Commons as one of its two dining halls and states that meal plans cover meals offered there.
cards.access_notes: Food requires payment or applicable meal-plan funds; confirm current dining service before visiting.

cards.title: Find the student center
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · food, seating, and a stage
cards.notes: Step into the Pilot House to orient yourself to a student-focused campus building. Keep it simple: meet up, sit down, and check posted programming.
cards.short_summary: A campus gathering spot with food-service options.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland’s international student guide describes the remodeled Pilot House as having a grill, small market, seating, pub, and stage for live entertainment.
cards.source_title: University of Portland International Student Guide
cards.access_notes: Food and market items require payment; choose all-ages programming and verify current event details.

cards.title: Check the Pilots After Dark listing
cards.subtitle: Friday or Saturday evening · student activity
cards.notes: Look for the current Pilots After Dark program through Student Activities. Pick an announced all-ages event and go with a new classmate or roommate.
cards.short_summary: Recurring student programming for Friday and Saturday evenings.
cards.evidence_claim: A 2025 University of Portland Student Affairs report states that more than 200 students attended Pilots After Dark events each Friday and Saturday evening.
cards.source_title: Division of Student Affairs Regents SAIE Committee Report, May 2025
cards.access_notes: Programming, locations, and any charges vary; check the current Student Activities listing before attending.

cards.title: Move between plans
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · recreation and wellness
cards.notes: Visit the recreation center for a low-pressure activity break. Check in with staff about current access, equipment availability, and any class schedules.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus option for indoor movement and wellness.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland describes the Beauchamp Recreation & Wellness Center as a two-story facility with cardio machines, weights, three basketball courts, an indoor track, and exercise studios.
cards.source_title: University of Portland International Student Guide
cards.access_notes: Access requirements and recreation schedules may vary; verify with the recreation center before visiting.

cards.title: Take a quiet architecture break
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Chapel of Christ the Teacher
cards.notes: Walk by the Chapel of Christ the Teacher and notice its Belluschi design. Use the stop for a few quiet minutes, respecting any worship or campus activity.
cards.short_summary: A documented campus landmark designed by Pietro Belluschi.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland’s digital collections state that the Chapel of Christ the Teacher was designed by Oregon architect Pietro Belluschi and dedicated on October 5, 1986.
cards.access_notes: Respect services and posted building-access guidance; access may be limited during events.

cards.title: Meet at the Bell Tower
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Bell Tower Plaza
cards.notes: Use the Bell Tower as an easy outdoor meeting point, then continue through the plaza toward the chapel and garden paths with your group.
cards.short_summary: A 106-foot campus landmark beside the chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland’s digital collections identify the Bell Tower as the tallest structure on campus at 106 feet.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; follow posted campus access guidance.

cards.title: Spot O Cruceiro by the library
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Clark Library approach
cards.notes: On the way around Clark Library, pause at O Cruceiro and read it as a campus wayfinding landmark. Keep the stop brief and pedestrian-friendly.
cards.short_summary: A granite campus path-marker near Clark Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Museum identifies O Cruceiro as a granite path-marker opposite the south steps of the Clark Library entrance.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus artwork; observe it from public walking paths.

cards.title: End with a riverfront walk
cards.subtitle: Sunday daytime · Cathedral Park, St. Johns
cards.notes: If you can arrange transportation, take a daytime walk on Cathedral Park’s paved paths and pause for Willamette River and St. Johns Bridge views.
cards.short_summary: A nearby city park with paved paths and riverfront views.
cards.evidence_claim: Portland Parks & Recreation lists Cathedral Park’s paved paths, riverfront views, picnic tables, and open hours of 5 a.m. to midnight.
cards.access_notes: Park hours are 5 a.m.–midnight. Stay on open paved paths and review the city’s current park notices before visiting.
